notes:
Inbound SMB lead via DSF webinar signup + quick product trial. Early discovery — self‑serve API key already created by CTO.

Summary / context:
- Product: NoteOrchard builds an in-app call summarization + searchable snippets layer for SMB sales teams. Customers upload call transcripts (auto transcribed) and user meta (caller name, account id) and get short bulleted summaries + embeddings for search.
- Doing a lightweight self-serve trial on Hosted API. Usage profile: mostly summarization and embeddings, occasional reranking at search time. Estimated monthly volume in POC: 6k–12k transcripts, avg transcript size ~2k tokens.
- Primary asks: can hosted API be used without Redwood retaining transcript text? Need explicit confirmation on retention window, ability to opt-out of logging/storage, and MFA/KMS details. CTO quote: "We love the API speed but can't have transcripts stored longer than 24 hours — and need a path for deletion audits."
- Compliance: SOC2 is a deal factor; also asking about EU data residency for specific customers (but initial deployment US-only). Wants audit logging and SSO for the console.

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2026-02-25: Lead created from webinar signup (source: webinar follow-up form). AE Jordan assigned.
- 2026-02-26: Trial API key generated (self-serve). First smoke tests performed by developer (low latency, small batch tests successful).
- 2026-03-01: Intro call with CTO + product manager (Fireflies ff-20260301-7a9c2b). CTO asked direct questions about retention, deletion APIs, and KMS options.
- 2026-03-03: AE sent initial security deck + hosted vs dedicated comparison. CTO replied with follow-up Qs re: retention SLA and audit trail for deletes.
- 2026-03-05: Security doc uploaded to Drive (NoteOrchard_Security_Reqs_2026-03-05.docx). SE Tara joined thread and proposed a short POC plan.
- 2026-03-12: Internal SE call to scope POC token limits and expected latency (target 250–400ms for summarization). Decided to map a 2‑week POC: 10k transcripts ingestion, retention policy test, and basic quality check.

POC requirements / acceptance criteria (from call):
- No persistent storage of raw transcripts beyond 24 hours unless explicitly opted-in.
- Ability to request proofs/records of deletion for at least last 30 days (audit log entries).
- Console SSO for admin access + audit logging of API key creation.
- Latency: p95 summarization <= 400ms for 2k-token transcripts.
- Cost sensitivity: target unit cost under $0.06/average transcript (comes from their internal pricing model).

Risks & blockers:
- Unclear whether Hosted API can meet strict non-retention requirement without Dedicated/private plan. CTO thinks hosted might be acceptable if retention controls are contractually guaranteed.
- Data residency for a subset of EU customers — they may later require EU-region processing (potential dedicated/private ask later).
- Need SOC2 documentation; marketing/legal review timeline could slow procurement.

Next steps (short):
- Action: Jordan to send a 1‑page hosted retention FAQ + example retention SLA clause by 2026-03-15.
- Action: Tara to prepare a minimal POC runbook (ingest flow, deletion verification steps) and propose start date 2026-03-22.
- If retention requirement can't be met on Hosted, propose a fast path to Dedicated pilot (cost estimate + minimal MSA).

Staging notes (AE shorthand):
- "Good fit for Hosted API if legal signs off on retention clause. CTO practical, cost-sensitive. Try to keep POC totally self-serve but ready to escalate to SE. Watch for EU residency ask."
- "Priority: retention SLA + deletion audit. If we can show delete proofs quickly, close likely in April (SMB, 12–24k ARR range)."
